key_insight: A multimodal temporal-attention deep learning model can detect hard-to-see welding defects in real time from synchronized images and sound, while also explaining which signals drive each prediction.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable in-line quality control for fillet-joint gas metal arc welding, reducing rework, production delays, and missed internal defects.
method: Trained a temporal attention-based deep learning classifier on welding images and acoustic data from an industrial collaborative robot.
Targeted internal defect classes including porosity, lack of penetration/fusion, undercut, and cold lap.
Used explainable AI to identify important regions in images and spectrograms and to compare modality usefulness by defect type.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the attention module improved the F1 score to 0.99 on the collected multimodal welding dataset.
watch_item: Performance is reported on a specific industrial setup, so generalization to other weld geometries, materials, sensors, or shop-floor noise conditions may require recalibration.
paper_title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data
